faq/agents:
Short answers on agent harnesses, model keys, and where agents run.

## Which agent harnesses are supported?

`claude-code`, `codex`, `osa`, and `custom`, set with `miosa agent new --harness`.
Agent Run providers also include `claude`, `pi`, and `hermes`.
See [Agents CLI](/docs/cli/agents) and [Configure an agent](/docs/guides/configure-agent).

## How do I create and run an agent?

```bash
miosa agent new reviewer --harness claude-code --instructions-file review.md
miosa agent run reviewer "review PR 42" --sandbox my-box
miosa run list                 # follow, stop
```

See [Agents CLI](/docs/cli/agents).

## What is OSA?

OSA is MIOSA's open-source agent.
It installs on your machine, runs as an MCP client, and runs headless with `osa run "..."` when you do not want the terminal UI.
See [MCP](/docs/mcp) and the [CLI reference](/docs/cli).

## Do agents use MIOSA platform keys?

No. Agents use your own model connections, never MIOSA platform keys.
Create an agent-scoped key and add a model connection before the first run.
See [Agents CLI](/docs/cli/agents).

## Where do agents run?

Agents work against a device: a Sandbox Worker, a Computer, or a local/BYOC device.
Docker Host is a hosting target, not an agent device.
See [Agent devices](/docs/guides/agent-devices) and [Choose an agent device](/docs/guides/agent-device-selection).

## Can I drive MIOSA from my own agent loop?

Yes. Call the primitives from your own backend, or start with the [Agent Development Kit (ADK)](/docs/adk).
See [Integrating an AI agent](/docs/guides/agent).
faq/browser-and-computer-use:
Short answers on browser automation, the computer-use loop, and live takeover.

## Where does browser automation run?

Inside a sandbox. The browser is part of the sandbox and starts lazily on the first browser request, then survives pause and resume.
See [Browser use](/docs/browser-use).

## What does starting a browser return?

A `stream_url` (live view), a `cdp_url` (Chrome DevTools Protocol), a one-hour `stream_auth` token, and a 1280x720 viewport.
Every sandbox image includes Chromium and Node, so any sandbox works.
See [Browser use quickstart](/docs/browser-use/quickstart).

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.miosa.ai/api/v1/sandboxes/$SANDBOX_ID/browser \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MIOSA_API_KEY"
```

## How does an agent attach to the browser?

Connect over CDP to the same browser a human can watch, so cookies and logins are shared.
Detach when you are done rather than calling `browser.close()`.
See [Drive the browser over CDP](/docs/browser-use/cdp).

## Can a human watch or take over a session?

Yes. Share a live viewer link for browser sessions, or take over a Computer desktop directly.
The live viewer needs the sandbox's virtual display, which a SOMA sandbox does not have yet.
See [Live viewer](/docs/browser-use/live-viewer) and [Embed a live desktop](/docs/computers/embedding).

## What is the computer-use loop?

Screenshot, decide, take one action, screenshot again.
Coordinates are screen pixels with the origin at the top left.
See [Computer use quickstart](/docs/computer-use/quickstart).

## How is browser and computer use billed?

Browser use bills as ordinary sandbox usage.
See [Browser use limits](/docs/browser-use/limits) and [Pricing and limits](/docs/pricing).
faq/business-os:
Short answers on running your own company on MIOSA and building an internal platform.

## Can I run my own company on MIOSA?

Yes. The reference map includes MIOSA BusinessOS, a self-hosted business workspace you run internally rather than launch as a product.
See [Agent company reference map](/docs/guides/agent-company-reference-map).

## How do agents reach my internal tools?

Managed connectors attach in-VM tools without shipping you vendor tokens; the sandbox gets a placeholder swapped only for that provider's endpoint.
See [Managed connectors](/docs/guides/managed-connectors).

## How do I pick a device for each job?

Pure reasoning needs no device; files and code use a Sandbox; browser and desktop work use a Computer; private customer resources use a local device; serving traffic uses Docker Host.
See [Choose an agent device](/docs/guides/agent-device-selection).

## Where do I start building an internal platform?

Follow the build-your-own-platform checklist: workspace, credentials, runtime profile, primary device, dispatch, stream, export, snapshot, publish, scale.
See [Build an agent-company platform](/docs/guides/build-agent-company).
faq/getting-started:
Short answers on the first steps with MIOSA.

Open a category, or use Expand all and Collapse all above the list.
Every question has its own link - the icon on the right - so you can share an answer directly.

## Where do I start?

The [Quickstart](/docs/quickstart) recommends **Track 1: sandbox to deployment** first.
Your first success is a site live at the production URL MIOSA returns, verified end to end.
The full walkthrough is [Build and deploy a Next.js app](/docs/learn/first-production-app).

## How do I authenticate?

With a MIOSA API key in an `Authorization: Bearer` header, or with a JWT from `POST /auth/login`.
See [Authentication](/docs/authentication) and [API keys](/docs/platform/api-keys).

## How do I install the CLI and sign in?

Install the `miosa` CLI (v2.2) from npm, Homebrew, the install script, or a release archive.
Then run `miosa login` for the device-code flow and `miosa whoami` to confirm the active organization and workspace.
See [Install the CLI](/docs/cli/install).

```bash
miosa login     # device-code flow
miosa whoami    # confirm the active organization and workspace
```

## How do I get an API key?

Create one under **Workspace → Settings → API Keys**.
The plaintext is shown once and only the hash is stored.
Key families are `msk_u_` (user), `msk_p_` (tenant platform), and `msk_a_` (operator admin, not self-service).
Default rates are 600 requests per minute for a user key and 30,000 for a platform key; rotate every 90 days.
See [API keys](/docs/platform/api-keys).

## Is there a test mode?

No.
There are no dedicated test-mode keys: `msk_u_*` and `msk_p_*` keys hit the billable production substrate.
Use a sandbox or a separate workspace for experiments.

## What IDs can I attach to a sandbox?

Free-form `metadata`, plus the queryable `external_user_id`, `external_workspace_id`, and `external_project_id`.
See [Metadata and labels](/docs/develop/sandboxes/metadata).

## Which regions exist, and can a sandbox move between them?

`us-west` (default), `us-east`, and `us-mia`, all generally available.
A resource lives in one region for its lifetime, so create one per region.
EU and APAC are on the roadmap.
See [Regions](/docs/regions).
faq/pricing-and-limits:
Short answers on what is billable, the sizes and caps, and how credits work.

## What am I billed for?

Running sandboxes and computers at the hourly price of their size, apps and databases on what they use (never more than the price of their size), paused storage, storage and egress, and builds.
The full list is on [Pricing and limits](/docs/pricing).

```bash
miosa usage my-box           # runtime, time left and estimated cost
```

## Do paused sandboxes cost anything?

Storage only. Billing for compute stops when the sandbox leaves `running`.
See [Sizing and limits](/docs/develop/sandboxes/sizing).

## What are the named sizes?

`xs` (1 vCPU, 2 GiB, 10 GiB) through `xl` (16 vCPU, 32 GiB, 80 GiB), with `small` as the default.
See [Sizing and limits](/docs/develop/sandboxes/sizing).

## What are the hard caps?

Concurrent sandboxes per plan (Developer 10, Business 250, Enterprise 500; upgrade or raise it through support), `timeout_sec` 1 to 86400, an 86,400 second maximum exec timeout, a 500 MB maximum upload, and a 1 hour browser token TTL.
See [Pricing and limits](/docs/pricing).

## What are the rate limits?

60 to 30,000 requests per minute per API key by tier, and 2,500/25,000/100,000 per minute per workspace on Developer/Business/Enterprise, with `429` and `Retry-After` on overrun.
See [Rate limits](/docs/rate-limits).

## How do I cap what one end user can spend?

The [Quotas API](/docs/api-reference/quotas) sets `max_sandboxes`, `max_concurrent`, `max_storage_gb`, and `max_credit_cents` per `external_user_id`, enforced at create time.

## How do I charge my own customers?

MIOSA bills you once; you charge your customers using attribution.
The [Usage Rollup API](/docs/api-reference/usage-rollup) groups by `external_user_id`, `external_project_id`, or `workspace_id`.
See [Usage and billing](/docs/platform/usage-and-billing).

## Do credits expire?

It depends on the grant.
Credits you add do not expire.
Recurring plan credits expire at the start of the UTC day after the 30-day billing period.
Promotional credits (the one-time welcome grant and promo-code redemptions) expire 180 days after they are granted.
The nearest expiry is reported as `credit_expiry_at` on `GET /api/v1/credits/balance`.
See [Pricing and limits](/docs/pricing).
faq/runtimes:
Short answers on the runtime you boot a sandbox on.

## What is SOMA?

SOMA (Secure Optimized Machine Architecture) is MIOSA's own open-source Rust VMM on Linux KVM, giving each sandbox one hardware-isolated VM with its own kernel.
See [SOMA](/docs/soma).

## How do I select a runtime?

Pass `runtime_profile: "standard" | "soma" | "auto"` when creating a sandbox, from the REST API, the SDKs (`runtime`), the CLI (`miosa create --runtime`), or the console.
An invalid value returns `INVALID_SANDBOX_RUNTIME_PROFILE`; there is no silent fallback.
`GET /api/v1/sandboxes/runtimes` lists the runtimes your organization can select.
See [Choosing a runtime](/docs/soma/choosing-a-runtime).

```bash
miosa create --runtime soma --size small
```

## Is SOMA available to everyone?

Yes. SOMA is available to every customer, at `small`, `medium`, and `large`, with live vCPU and memory resize.
`GET /api/v1/sandboxes/runtimes` reports what each runtime supports today.
See [SOMA](/docs/soma).

## What is generally available and what is in preview?

Sandboxes, previews, publishing, data, white-label, SOMA, and the sandbox browser are generally available.
Computers, dynamic deployments, Docker Host, and tenant deployment domains are in partner preview; GPU-backed sandboxes are not productized and remain on the roadmap.
See [Availability and roadmap](/docs/availability).
faq/sandboxes-and-computers:
## Sandbox or Computer?

Use a [Sandbox](/docs/develop/sandboxes) for code, files, and processes.
Use a [Computer](/docs/computers/overview) when you need a visible desktop, a browser login, or human takeover.
Use **Docker Host** when you need a durable, always-on URL.

```bash
miosa create my-box --wait     # provision a sandbox and wait until it is ready
miosa list                     # see all your sandboxes
```

## What do I get in a default sandbox?

A headless microVM that is persistent by default, with `/workspace` as the editable root, booted from a template (usually `miosa-sandbox`).
The default size `small` is 2 vCPU, 4096 MiB RAM, and 10240 MiB disk, and responses carry a versioned `resource_contract`.
See [Sandboxes](/docs/develop/sandboxes) and [Sizing and limits](/docs/develop/sandboxes/sizing).

## What is different about a Computer?

A Computer is a durable cloud Linux desktop (Xfce and Firefox) with screenshot, click, type, and streaming, plus human takeover.
You embed or share it through `computer.urls()["desktop_url"]`.
See [Computers](/docs/computers/overview) and [Embed a live desktop](/docs/computers/embedding).

## How long can a sandbox run?

`timeout_sec` is 1 to 86400 seconds, default 3600.
`always_on` disables timeout enforcement subject to tenant policy.
The timeout counts from the last activity, and expiry stops a persistent sandbox and destroys a non-persistent one.
A sandbox also stops after 30 minutes idle by default on accounts created on or after October 11, 2026 (set `idle_timeout_sec` to `0` to disable), and a stopped sandbox wakes on the next request.
See [Timeouts and auto-stop](/docs/develop/sandboxes/timeouts).

## What are the sandbox states?

`creating`, `running`, `stopped`, `paused`, `error`, and `destroyed`.
`paused` exists only on a runtime that advertises pause, which is Firecracker today; SOMA has no pause.
See [Sandbox lifecycle](/docs/develop/sandboxes/lifecycle).

## Does stopping a sandbox lose my files?

No. Stop keeps the sandbox id and the disk, including files, installed packages, and enabled services; resume brings it back.
Stop never keeps running processes.
Pause (Firecracker only) keeps processes for up to 30 minutes, then behaves like a stop.
Persistent means the sandbox survives a stop, not the loss of its host; the `durability` field says how many hosts hold the saved state.
SOMA does not support persistence, pause, or snapshots yet.
Destroy is what removes saved state.
See [Snapshots and persistence](/docs/develop/snapshots).

## What is the difference between a snapshot and a fork?

Restore builds a new sandbox from a checkpoint; fork branches a running sandbox into an independent one.
Both leave the source unchanged.
See [Snapshots and persistence](/docs/develop/snapshots).

```bash
miosa snapshot save my-box before-upgrade   # pin a named restore point
miosa snapshot fork before-upgrade          # branch it into an independent sandbox
```

## Does a snapshot save my database?

No. A snapshot captures the sandbox disk and, where the runtime advertises it, memory only.
External databases, object storage, connectors, and third-party services are not rolled back with it.
Keep durable state in a data service.
See [Data overview](/docs/data/overview).
faq/security-and-compliance:
Short answers on certifications, data location, secrets, and retention.

## Are you SOC 2 compliant?

Not yet. Our SOC 2 audit is in progress and not complete, so there is no report to share today.
Until it is issued, we can share our security questionnaire and controls documentation under NDA.
See [Trust](https://miosa.ai/trust) for the current status.

## Do you support HIPAA?

MIOSA runs HIPAA-compliant infrastructure for healthcare workloads, and business associate agreements (BAAs) are available for Enterprise customers.
See [Trust](https://miosa.ai/trust).

## Where does my data live?

In United States data centers we provision, network, and manage directly; MIOSA is not a reseller of a hyperscaler.
The three live regions are all in the US, and a resource cannot move between them after creation.
See [Regions](/docs/regions) and [Trust](https://miosa.ai/trust).

## How are secrets stored?

Values are encrypted with ChaCha20-Poly1305.
Sandboxes see an opaque `miosa-tok-<hex>` placeholder that is swapped at egress, so no one - including MIOSA engineers - can re-read a stored value.
See [Secrets](/docs/security/secrets).

## How long is data retained?

Egress audit events are retained 90 days.
Usage and credit records are kept separately.
There is no published zero-retention mode.
See [Data retention](/docs/data-retention).

## Are there publishable keys for the browser?

No. There are no `pk_*` publishable keys: API keys are server-only.
Browser and embed access uses short-lived scoped tokens instead (`mp_` preview, `ms_` share, and browser tokens).
See [API keys](/docs/platform/api-keys) and [Browser tokens](/docs/platform/browser-tokens).
faq/support:
Short answers on reaching the team and following platform changes.

## How do I get help?

Open an in-product ticket from the dashboard - the fastest path for anything involving a resource - or email support@miosa.ai for non-resource questions.
See [Support](/docs/support).

## What should I include in a request?

The resource id, the operation you ran, a timestamp with timezone, the `x-request-id`, and the exact error message.
See [Support](/docs/support).

## Where can I see status and changes?

The status page for live health, the [changelog](/docs/changelog) for shipped changes, and [Known limitations](/docs/known-limitations) for current gaps.
See [Support](/docs/support).

## Where is the community?

Join the MIOSA Discord for questions and announcements.

## Still stuck?

- [Ask OSA](/docs/support): Ask OSA is built into every docs page - use the button in the header for instant answers grounded in these docs.
- [Email support](mailto:support@miosa.ai): Open a ticket from the dashboard, or email the support address. Include the resource id, operation, timestamp, x-request-id, and exact error.
- [Join Discord](https://discord.gg/miosa): Ask in the MIOSA Discord, where the team and other builders hang out.
faq/white-label:
Short answers on running MIOSA under your own brand for your customers.

## How does white-label work on MIOSA?

Your platform maps to one MIOSA organization, with a workspace per downstream customer and a project per thing they build.
End users never need a MIOSA account.
See [White-label platform architecture](/docs/platform/overview).

## What branded URLs can I use?

A preview domain (`https://{port}-{slug}.sandbox.{preview_domain}`), a deployment domain (`https://{slug}.{deployment_domain}`), and a MIOSA fallback (`https://{slug}.{organization_slug}.miosa.app`).
See [Branding and domain setup](/docs/platform/white-label).

## How do my end users authenticate?

Never put an `msk_*` key in a browser.
Your backend mints short-lived scoped tokens, and end-user-scoped secrets and OAuth are keyed on `external_user_id`.
See [Attribution](/docs/platform/attribution) and [White-label credentials](/docs/security/white-label).

## How do I bill my customers through MIOSA?

MIOSA charges the organization owner for all usage in one bill.
Charge back to customers by grouping the Usage Rollup on `workspace_id` or the `external_*` fields.
See [Usage and billing](/docs/platform/usage-and-billing).

## Can I brand the console and desktop?

Yes. Set `custom_app_name`, `custom_logo_url`, `support_url`, `desktop_wallpaper_url`, and `powered_by_visible` through `PUT /api/v1/tenant/branding`.
See [Branding and domain setup](/docs/platform/white-label).
